newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks seen lower ahead of Monday audit.
newsitem.headline: French stocks seen lower ahead of Monday audit.

text.p: French shares were expected to open lower on Friday ahead of the release on Monday of an audit of public finances and under pressure from technical factors, dealers said.
"The market corrected well yesterday and can continue to do so while waiting for the audit on Monday," a trader said. "The outlook for a rise in the corporate tax will weigh on the whole market."

A source close to the government said on Thursday that the government was studying raising corporate tax and increasing company social security contributions to help plug a budget deficit expected at around 3.6 percent of gross domestic product.
* CAC-40 Jul futures 2,953 vs 2,966 at Thursdays close.

* Club Med announced a first half 1996/1997 net loss 413 million francs after 630 million francs of charges. The company also warned of more charges in the second half, but said they would be lower than in the first six months.
The company said that in spite of the loss its financial situation remains healthy with financial debt limited to 2.4 billion francs for 3.5 billion francs shareholder's equity.
On the technical front, the outlook is bearish with support seen at 2,950, 2,925 and 2,900 for the future.
In the cash market, Crredit Agricole futures' target was 2,932 for the session with a support test at 2,915 if the previous level failed to hold.
If the index sticks at those levels, the upside target is 2,960/2,977, Credit Agricole said.
"The market reached its target of 3,000 points yesterday, now it will consolidate, or even correct before doing better in the medium term," a trader said.
